prompt: The density of a certain type of basalt is $685$ kilograms per cubic meter. A sample of this basalt is in the shape of a cube, where each edge has a length of $0.80$ meters. To the nearest whole number, what is the mass, in kilograms, of this sample?
explanation: Choice A is correct. The sample is in the shape of a cube with edge length $0.80$ meters, so its volume is $0.80^{3}$, or $0.512$, cubic meters. Since the density is $685$ kilograms per $1$ cubic meter, the mass of the sample is $\left(0.512 \text{ cubic meters}\right)\left(\frac{685 \text{ kilograms}}{1 \text{ cubic meter}}\right)$, or $350.72$ kilograms. Rounded to the nearest whole number, the mass is $351$ kilograms.
